note.text:
The calorific (energy) value of a food is the energy one gram of it gives the body. It is measured in kilojoules (kJ) or kilocalories (kcal); 1 kcal ≈ 4.2 kJ.
Energy values: fat about 37 kJ per gram, carbohydrate about 17 kJ per gram, protein about 17 kJ per gram. Fat gives about twice as much energy as the others.
Energy from a food = mass (g) × energy per gram.
Experiment: burn a known mass of food (a groundnut) under a tube of water. The heat taken in by the water = mass of water (g) × 4.2 × temperature rise (J). Dividing by the mass of food gives the energy per gram. The result is lower than the true value because some heat escapes into the air.

worked_example.problem: How much energy is in {g} g of fat ({e} kJ per gram)?

cards.idea: Fat gives about {37} kJ per gram; carbohydrate and protein about {17} kJ per gram.
example: Fat gives about twice as much energy.
Groundnuts and palm oil are rich in fat.

cards.idea: Energy from a food = mass (g) × energy per gram.
example: Check the units: g × kJ per g = kJ.

check.prompt: How much energy is in {g} g of {X.n} ({X.e} kJ per gram)?

misconceptions.explain: Multiply the mass by the energy per gram.

cards.idea: Heat taken in by water = mass of water (g) × {4.2} × temperature rise (J).
example: Some heat escapes, so the result is too low.

check.prompt: A groundnut of mass {f} g is burned under a tube holding {w} g of water. The water's temperature rises by {t} °C. How much heat did the water take in (in J)?

misconceptions.explain: Multiply by {4.2} too (the energy to warm {1} g of water by {1} °C).
Use the mass of the water, not of the groundnut.

solution: Heat = mass of water × {4.2} × temperature rise.

pick.q: Which food type gives the most energy per gram?
e: Protein gives about 17 kJ per gram.
Carbohydrate gives about 17 kJ per gram.
pick.y: Fat gives about 37 kJ per gram.

pick.q: In what unit is the energy value of food measured?
pick.y: Energy is measured in joules or kilojoules.
